story.head: Stay out of the box, Blue Jackets
paras: The Blue Jackets (8-12-0) beat Chicago 4-2 on Thursday, while the Devils (15-7-0) lost 3-2 to Montréal on Wednesday. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Jackets seventh (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Devils second (tied for eighth).

The Blue Jackets have played better than their record (.400) says: their chances are worth about .492, and their finishing has held them back. The Devils’ record (.682) is about what their chances are worth.

The Blue Jackets forecheck as hard as almost anyone (3rd) and do a lot of their shooting from distance (3rd lowest). They also get their defensemen shooting (3rd), so their defensemen shoot a lot, and the Devils’ not so much. Columbus has scored 2.40 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Devils rarely throw hits (2nd lowest), draw more penalties than they take (3rd) and keep things calm after the whistle (3rd lowest). The Devils’ power play (5th) could do real damage against the Blue Jackets’ penalty kill (23rd).

Kent Johnson (9 G / 12 A / 21 P in 20 GP) leads the Blue Jackets in scoring, and Zach Werenski (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 20 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Devils, Jack Hughes (10 G / 17 A / 27 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in five straight games against Columbus. Jesper Bratt (4 G / 18 A / 22 P in 22 GP) isn’t far behind.
Cam Talbot (6-4-0 / .907 SV% in 10 GS) is in line to start for Columbus. Connor Hellebuyck (7-1-0 / .913 SV% in 8 GS) has been terrific for New Jersey and will likely start.
